title: Advice Will Always Be Human | Emmelia Powell
summary: Advice Will Always Be Human | Emmelia Powell - A Saturn Studios original following advisers who blend technology with humanity to transform financial advice.
body_text: Whilst we build collaboratively with our partners, we continue to realise just how much financial advice is and has always been about people. Beyond the admin and regulation, its real connection, value, and empathy that allows advisers to guide clients through life’s complexity. These are all stories that Saturn exists to support and share. “If you can make the mundane more efficient, you have more time to explore leadership, to have human connections, to be creative thinkers, to be problem solvers, and go out to see clients face to face.” – Emmelia Powell advises. ‘Advice Will Always Be Human’ is an original Saturn Studios production that will follow a series of advisers to hear about their stories so far and how they’re integrating technology into their businesses to make a tangible difference to peoples lives. Delivered with Emmelia’s characteristic candour and passion to serve other human beings as they navigate their lives and finances. Emmelia cuts through the noise and breaks down the challenges Premier Wealth Solution’s faces, how technology enables them to service the mundane, and how advice should be delivered. Amal Jolly, Saturn CEO, said: “Behind every financial plan is a human story. Advisers and their teams quietly change lives, giving families confidence and peace of mind. By sharing these powerful personal stories, we show a future where it can scale to hundreds of millions while staying human at its core, amplified by technology. Advice Will Always Be Human will continue with the story of Rory Albon.

title: Acumen Pharmaceuticals Highlights Enhanced Brain Delivery™ (EBD™) Program Data and Early Alzheimer’s Disease Insights at the Alzheimer’s Association International Conference (AAIC®) 2026
summary: EBD™ bispecific antibodies targeting both AβOs and hTfR showed improved brain penetration compared to the native anti-AβO antibodies, which may enable administration with a low-volume delivery device and reduce the delivered dose required for efficacy EBD candidate ACU401 achieves up to 40-fold
body_text: Acumen Pharmaceuticals Highlights Enhanced Brain Delivery™ (EBD™) Program Data and Early Alzheimer’s Disease Insights at the Alzheimer’s Association International Conference (AAIC®) 2026 July 15, 2026 at 7:30 AM EDT PDF Version EBD™ bispecific antibodies targeting both AβOs and hTfR showed improved brain penetration compared to the native anti-AβO antibodies, which may enable administration with a low-volume delivery device and reduce the delivered dose required for efficacy EBD candidate ACU401 achieves up to 40-fold greater frontal cortex exposure in non-human primates and significant increase in exposures in deep brain regions No hematological safety signals observed in non-human primates, demonstrating low potential for anemia ALTITUDE-AD patient experience data highlight unmet need in early Alzheimer's disease NEWTON, Mass., July 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Acumen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: ABOS) (Acumen), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics that target soluble amyloid beta oligomers (AβOs) for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), today announced new findings presented at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference (AAIC®) 2026 in London. Following collaboration with JCR Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. (JCR) on EBD candidate development, studies demonstrated improved brain penetration of anti-AβO antibodies through transferrin receptor-mediated delivery across both mouse and non-human primate models. Additionally, research from early symptomatic AD patients highlighted the lived experience among ALTITUDE-AD trial participants and their study partners. “Confirming our mouse data in non-human primates is a pivotal step for our EBD program," said Paul Shughrue, PhD, Vice President, Program Leader and Head of Research, Acumen Pharmaceuticals. “The degree of brain penetration we observed in cynomolgus monkeys, combined with preserved soluble amyloid beta oligomer selectivity and a clean hematological profile, exceeded our expectations and gives us strong confidence in the differentiated potential of our EBD program’s approach.” Acumen’s presentation details are as follows: Utilizing the Transferrin Receptor-Mediated Transport System for Enhanced Brain Delivery of anti-Aβ Oligomer Antibodies To evaluate transferrin receptor (TfR)-mediated brain delivery, Acumen and JCR developed and characterized anti-AβO antibody fusion proteins incorporating J-Brain Cargo®, JCR’s clinically validated platform targeting the TfR, to facilitate brain uptake in humanized TfR mice. Fusion with anti-TfR fragments did not alter AβO affinity or selectivity. All EBD constructs achieved substantially higher brain levels than native anti-AβO antibodies, with each construct displaying a unique pharmacokinetic profile. Systemic absorption was confirmed after subcutaneous dosing and constructs retained the ability to bind Aβ species of interest in human AD brain tissue. These findings support the continued advancement of lead EBD candidates and efforts to advance a construct to clinical trials. Bispecific Antibodies that Bind Aβ Oligomers and Transferrin Receptors Show Enhanced Brain Delivery in Cynomolgus Monkeys In collaboration with JCR, Acumen evaluated three bispecific antibodies fusing anti-AβO antibody (ACU234) with anti-TfR antibody fragments in cynomolgus monkeys. After intravenous dosing, all three bispecific antibodies achieved greater brain exposure than ACU234 alone, with at least 14-fold higher levels in the frontal cortex. Candidate molecule ACU401 demonstrated particularly robust brain penetration: 22-fold higher at 3 hours and 40-fold higher at 24 hours in the frontal cortex, with similar trends observed in the hippocampus and putamen. No hematological findings suggestive of anemia were observed. These results, together with evidence of systemic absorption after subcutaneous dosing, highlight the potential of EBD molecules for further development in early AD. Understanding Early Symptomatic Alzheimer’s Disease Through Patient Perspectives: Findings from the ALTITUDE-AD Clinical Trial Population Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 38 participants and their study partners prior to treatment in the ALTITUDE-AD Phase 2 study. Participants described pervasive memory-related challenges including forgetfulness, difficulty completing tasks, and communication difficulties. Emotional impacts, frustration, worry, and reduced confidence contributed to social withdrawal and reduced activity participation. Participants also reported actively managing others’ perceptions of their symptoms through masking and selective disclosure. Together, results illustrate the diverse ways individuals with early Alzheimer's disease experience, respond to, and cope with cognitive and functional changes, underscoring the importance of capturing patient experience directly to better understand meaningful benefit at this stage of disease. “Two of the most persistent challenges in Alzheimer's drug development are getting therapeutics where they need to go in the brain and truly understanding what matters to patients living with the disease,” said Eric Siemers, M.D., Chief Medical Officer of Acumen Pharmaceuticals. “The data we've presented at AAIC speaks directly to both. Our collaborative work with JCR continues to push the boundaries of what's possible with brain delivery, while our patient experience findings remind us why this work matters so deeply.” The data posters presented will be available on the Company’s website at: https://acumenpharm.com/publications/ . About Sabirnetug (ACU193) Sabirnetug (ACU193) is a humanized monoclonal antibody (mAb) discovered and developed based on its selectivity for soluble amyloid beta oligomers (AβOs), which are a highly toxic and pathogenic form of Aβ, relative to Aβ monomers and amyloid plaques. Soluble AβOs have been observed to be potent neurotoxins that bind to neurons, inhibit synaptic function and induce neurodegeneration. By selectively targeting toxic soluble AβOs, sabirnetug aims to address the hypothesis that soluble AβOs are an early and persistent underlying cause of the neurodegenerative process in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Sabirnetug has been granted Fast Track designation for the treatment of early AD by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and is currently being evaluated in a Phase 2 study in patients with early AD. About ALTITUDE-AD (Phase 2) Initiated in 2024, ALTITUDE-AD is a Phase 2, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of sabirnetug (ACU193) infusions administered once every four weeks in slowing cognitive and functional decline as compared to placebo in participants with early Alzheimer's disease. The study has enrolled 542 individuals with early Alzheimer’s disease (mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to AD) at multiple investigative sites located in the United States, Canada, the European Union and the United Kingdom. Topline results are expected in late 2026. More information can be found on www.clinicaltrials.gov, NCT identifier NCT06335173. About Acumen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Acumen Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing a novel therapeutic that targets toxic soluble amyloid beta oligomers (AβOs) for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Acumen’s scientific founders pioneered research on AβOs, which a growing body of evidence indicates are early and persistent triggers of Alzheimer’s disease pathology. Acumen is currently focused on advancing its investigational product candidate, sabirnetug (ACU193), a humanized monoclonal antibody that selectively targets toxic soluble AβOs, in its ongoing Phase 2 clinical trial ALTITUDE-AD (NCT06335173) in early symptomatic AD, following positive results in its Phase 1 trial INTERCEPT-AD. Acumen is investigating a subcutaneous formulation of sabirnetug using Halozyme’s proprietary ENHANZE® drug delivery technology. Acumen is also collaborating with JCR Pharmaceuticals to develop an Enhanced Brain Delivery™ (EBD™)-enabled therapy for Alzheimer’s disease utilizing a transferrin-receptor-targeting blood-brain barrier-penetrating technology. The company is headquartered in Newton, Mass. For more information, visit www.acumenpharm.com . About the J-Brain Cargo® Platform Technology JCR Pharmaceuticals has developed a proprietary blood-brain barrier (BBB)-penetrating technology, J-Brain Cargo®, to bring biotherapeutics into the central nervous system (CNS). The first drug developed based on this technology is IZCARGO™ (INN: pabinafusp alfa) and is approved in Japan for the treatment of a lysosomal storage disorder. About JCR Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. JCR Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. is a global specialty pharmaceutical company that develops treatments that go beyond rare diseases to solve the world’s most complex healthcare challenges. JCR continues to build upon our 50-year legacy in Japan while expanding our global footprint into the US, Europe, and Latin America. JCR’s innovative therapies in Japan address conditions like growth disorder, MPS II (Hunter syndrome), Fabry disease, acute graft-versus-host disease, and renal anemia. JCR is also advancing the global development for rare diseases like MPS I (Hurler, Hurler-Scheie and Scheie syndrome), MPS II, MPS IIIA and B (Sanfilippo syndrome type A and B), and more. For more information, visit https://jcrpharm.com/ . body_text: Your business is moving faster than ever. You’ve streamlined your supply chain, digitised your operations, and expanded your reach to new markets. Today, modern, digital fintechs are creating new opportunities, especially in the emerging markets, for small and medium businesses to trade freely and scale their operations. How fast is trade moving across Africa? At nearly £25 billion, UK to -Africa trade recorded an annual growth rate of roughly 7%. The UK maintains nine trade agreements covering 18 African nations, including roll-over economic partnership agreements (EPAs) and trading blocs. When trade volumes increase, payment speed needs to match. Yet, for many business owners, the reality involves weeks of waiting for onboarding documentation to clear, manual forms, and outdated approval cycles. This friction creates a significant hurdle, turning agile opportunities into stalled growth. To compete in today’s landscape, SMEs need to rethink how they manage cross-border payments. For businesses in the UK, time is the most valuable currency. Every day spent waiting on documentation or clearance in emerging markets is a day your business isn't moving products or settling invoices with key suppliers. How optimised payments protect SME margins Modern financial solutions are now prioritising straight-through processing for local businesses. By focusing on digital-first verification, your business can now bypass the traditional waiting game. When you remove the administrative bottlenecks, you regain the ability to execute trades instantly, ensuring your cash flow stays as dynamic as your business strategy. Remove the payment layers Hidden fees and FX markups silently kill SME profitability as conventional payment routes often come with 3-5% margins that erode your bottom line before the money even arrives at its destination. The currency fluctuations between the UK and Africa widen the gap that only increases with the payment layers. Instead, businesses should invest in infrastructure that can reduce this gap and the payment frictions. Invest in transparent infrastructure Protecting your profits shouldn’t be complex. When your payment costs are predictable and transparent, you have a clearer picture of your actual operational costs. Payment workflow that allows competitive FX rates and transparency lets you keep more revenue in your business. The next era of African commerce is powered by a digital financial infrastructure , purpose-built to offer the agility required by SMEs and the scale demanded by large-scale enterprises. Reduce operational overload True operational autonomy means having the ability to pay anyone, anywhere, without geographical limitations. Relying on fragmented, slow payment systems that only work on weekdays limits your ability to enter new markets or onboard new suppliers. A digital payment system can reduce the overload and provide the agility to your business. Read the Comprehensive guide to cross border payments Turn your payment process into a competitive advantage Success for SMEs in today’s market is won with agility, where less time is spent managing the "how" of your payments and it’s focused on growing your business, improving your product, and serving your customers. By prioritising payment speed, demanding transparent costs, and utilising digital-first payment infrastructure, you can turn your financial operations into a strategic advantage. A modern digital infrastructure allows you to maintain multi-currency wallets and execute cross-border payments with the same ease as local transactions. In order to expand your footprint without the constant fear of payment delays or currency conversion hurdles, it’s wise to invest in an efficient payments system. It should offer multiple countries and payout across the globe with transparent FX fees and clear visibility of cash movements. The future of trade belongs to those who can move as fast as the market demands. With the right tools, your payment processes can finally catch up. title: EV Chassis: The Complete Guide to Electric Vehicle Platforms
summary: Everything you need to know about EV chassis design, skateboard platforms, and modular electric vehicle construction.
body_text: An EV chassis is the biggest shift in automotive design since we stopped using horses. What Is an EV Chassis? A complete rolling foundation with everything electric built in: battery, motor, cooling, controls, safety systems. Unlike traditional chassis that need an engine added, an EV chassis arrives functional and ready to drive. What's Included 42-54 kWh battery pack in the floor Electric motor and single-speed transmission Power electronics and charging systems Thermal management for battery and motor Suspension, brakes, steering Safety systems and crash protection Vehicle computer and software Cockpit with display and HVAC The Olympus platform: complete integration, drives under its own power Why Skateboard Design Works "Skateboard" describes the shape: flat battery deck with wheels at corners. This puts the heaviest component (battery) as low as possible. Key Benefits Low center of gravity: Battery inches off the ground means less body roll, better handling. Perfect weight distribution: Batteries spread across entire floor for 50/50 balance front to rear. Flat interior floor: No engine, no transmission tunnel, no driveshaft. Maximum interior space. Battery System The battery pack is structural. It's part of the chassis, not cargo. The enclosure carries loads and adds rigidity. This saves weight by eliminating redundant structure. Inside the Pack Thousands of lithium-ion cells grouped into modules. Battery Management System monitors every module for voltage, temp, and health. Liquid cooling keeps everything in the optimal 20-40°C range. Motor Configuration Olympus uses a single rear motor. 174 HP continuous. Permanent magnet motor for high efficiency. Single-speed reduction gear, no multi-speed transmission needed. Why single-speed? Electric motors deliver full torque from zero RPM and maintain power to 15,000+ RPM. No shifting required. Digital Controls Drive-by-wire eliminates mechanical linkages. Steering and braking are electronic. This enables: Adjustable steering feel via software One-pedal driving with regen braking Traction control and torque vectoring Remote operation capability Commercial Applications Fleet Vehicles Delivery companies mount different cargo bodies on the same electric platform. One powertrain across the fleet simplifies maintenance. Custom Manufacturers Small manufacturers building specialty vehicles use the chassis to avoid developing powertrains. Focus on body design and features. Autonomous Development Drive-by-wire and digital controls make the platform ideal for autonomous systems. Connect via CAN bus and control everything electronically. Olympus Specs 174 HP Continuous Power 42-54 kWh Battery Capacity 155-255 mi Range 3,550 lbs Payload Full Specifications Platform Skateboard with structural battery Motor 130 kW (174 HP continuous) Charging DC fast + Level 2 AC Wheelbase 183-196" adjustable Top Speed 121 mph Controls Drive-by-wire FAQs How much does it cost to build with an EV chassis? ▼ Building from scratch costs $500M-$2B and 4-5 years. Using a pre-engineered EV chassis reduces costs by 60-80% and cuts time to 12-18 months. Why don't EVs need multi-speed transmissions? ▼ Electric motors deliver full torque from 0 RPM to 15,000+ RPM. A single-speed gear handles all situations. Simpler, lighter, more reliable. What's the advantage of skateboard design? ▼ Low center of gravity, 50/50 weight distribution, and flat interior floor with no transmission tunnel. Can it be used for autonomous vehicles? ▼ Yes. Drive-by-wire controls make it ideal for autonomous systems. Connect via CAN bus and control everything electronically. Summary The Olympus EV Chassis is available now. Certified, tested, and ready for your vehicle design. Whether you're building fleet vehicles, custom vehicles, or autonomous platforms, the skateboard architecture gives you a proven foundation.

title: Markets Stay Mixed Again; Crude Continues to Price Down
summary: Cboe Global Markets, a leading provider of market infrastructure and tradable products, delivers cutting-edge trading, clearing and investment solutions to market participants around the world.
body_text: Article published at 9:15 a.m. CT JJ Kinahan is Senior Vice President, Head of Retail Expansion and Alternative Investment Products at Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (Cboe). Key Takeaways: Crude oil prices drop on hopes of peace pact Tech stocks pressure Nasdaq early on Earnings out from Sherwin-Williams, Coca-Cola and Johnson & Johnson The markets are mixed again in early trading with the Nasdaq Composite under pressure after yesterday’s chip maker fallout that also pushed down tech shares in South Korea and Europe. In fact, it was the third worst day in Soth Korea’s KOSPI index history. Crude oil prices are also dropping as hopes of diplomacy between the U.S. and Iran grow after the two paused strikes in recent days. WTI Crude Oil prices were off by 1.8% to the lower $81 range. Yesterday, WTI crude saw its largest one-day drop in two months, ending the session at $81.77, down 8.5%. The Nasdaq Composite is heading lower by nearly 0.59% and the S&P 500 Index is floating just above the flat line. The Dow Jones Industrial Average is edging up at 0.93%. Yesterday’s trading was a mishmash. Out of the gate, stocks were turning higher only to finish close to the flat line and even a smidge below. The Dow finished up 0.51%, helped by crude oil’s fall while the Nasdaq backtracked by 0.18, hurt by chip makers. In the meantime, the S&P barely budged, off 0.02% at the close. The tech retraction also hit South Korean semiconductor shares of SK Hynix, falling 14%, and Samsung Electronics tumbling 13%. Among the U.S.-based tech stocks, Micron Technology was treading lower by 6.8% in early trading while Nvidia shares were off 0.50%. Broadcom shares backtracked by 2.1% and Taiwan Semiconductor were off by 3.5%. Sherwin-Williams shares were helping boost both the S&P and the Dow after the paint maker reported earnings and revenues that beat Wall Street expectations, thanks somewhat to a successful 8% higher price point in its paint stores group to help offset inflation. The company also touted acquisitions and new orders and raised its forward guidance. Shares were higher by 6.6%. Coca-Cola shares are up nearly 2.5% in early trading after the beverage and snacks maker turned in second-quarter profits and revenues that outstripped Wall Street’s estimates. The results were driven by an uptick in beverage sales, particularly zero-sugar drinks and the fairlife milk brand, coupled with higher prices. Coca-Cola also noted that global consumption grew during the FIFA World Cup. Boeing reported a wider-than-expected loss, but revenues were better than Wall Street’s expectations. The airplane maker took a one-time charge of $280 million for Air Force One development, which has rung up a number of cost overruns on what has become a $4 billion project. What also caught investor’s interest was that free cash flow of $631 million was far ahead of the outlook of a negative number. Boeing also confirmed its full-year guidance of free cash flow in the $1 billion to $3 billion range. Shares fell early on but were moving to the upside by about 1.4% in recent action. Johnson & Johnson shares were headed to the upside by nearly 2% after the drug maker agreed to pay $5.5 billion to settle the remaining talc lawsuits. The lawsuits claiming that talc products caused ovarian cancer first began 15 years ago with one lawsuit that led to a landslide of others. The settlement is conditioned on at 95% of the remaining claimants accept it. UPS’s years-long realignment is paying off after the delivery giant raised its full-year outlook after reporting earnings that were below the year-ago results but outpaced Wall Street’s expectations. The company touted its fourth straight quarter of better-than-expected results. The Federal Reserve’s two-day meeting starts today with an interest rate decision set for tomorrow afternoon. The CME’s FedWatch tool is projecting a 31.5% probability of a rate hike. Keep an eye out for Visa’s earnings after the bell. The global payment tech firm is expected to post robust earnings and revenues supported by a “FIFA bump.” Last week Visa reported that its status as the exclusive payment services sponsor of the FIFA World Cup drove a 20% boost across cross-border payments, particularly in host cities such as Boston and New York. There’s a 3.5% implied stock movement in either direction after the results are posted. As noted above, Nvidia shares are falling again today following yesterday’s 5% tumble to $196.51. The pullback was prompted by reports that it will finance some $250 billion to OpenAI. That follows Friday’s announcement that it is in a $500 billion partnership with SK Hynix to codevelop AI factory construction for next-generation AI memory supply. The $750 billion worth of partnerships is raising concerns about “circular” financing in which suppliers are major investors in their customers. If the program goes through – and it’s still not secured – Nvidia would allow the ChatGPT maker to borrow at reduced rates. Nvidia’s selling, coupled with Apple’s record-high closing at $336.91, had the two switching places as the most valuable publicly held company. Apple – on pace for its best month in four years – closed just shy of $5 trillion market capitalization at $4.948 trillion. Nvidia dropped to second place with market cap at $4.760 trillion. The next top three market cap leaders are Alphabet at $3.994 trillion, Microsoft at $2.890 trillion and Amazon at $2.489 trillion. Apple, which doesn’t have an integrated AI program, also hit a fresh intraday peak at $339.57. Apple shares rose nearly 20% in the last month and is up 58% in the last year. title: The Bathroom Remodeler's Guide to Voice & SMS AI
summary: How voice and SMS AI help bathroom remodeling companies answer every lead, cover every hour, and book more appointments without adding headcount.
body_text: By Pam Torrey , Senior Director of Marketing at Leaping AI A homeowner is sitting in their living room at 9:40 on a Tuesday night, exhausted from bath time with two kids because their old tub isn’t set up for a modern family. She then goes online and fills out a quote form for a bathroom remodel that goes to three local remodelers. Whoever calls back first is most likely to win the job. That’s not a guess, rather it’s based on real data that tells us most homeowners go with the first contractor they speak to, regardless of price. That’s how the one-day bath industry has worked for years and it’s the reason the phone matters so much in this vertical. Before a homeowner fills out a quote form on a website, they’ve most likely spent time on Google, checking out top ranking remodelers, comparing reviews, and narrowing the list down to two or three they’d like to hear from. By the time they submit a form or dial a phone number, they’re not just casually looking for a contractor. They are ready to talk to someone about what they need, what it will cost, and when it can be installed. The remodeler who reaches them first with a real answer to those questions will usually get the appointment and later, the sale. Bathroom remodeling occupies an unusual spot in the home improvement industry. The average ticket size is enough that homeowners generally shop around, often getting two or three quotes before they commit to a contractor. Because of the size and scope of the purchase, homeowners will research when they have time, maybe even weeks or months before submitting for a quote. And the market is crowded enough that companies selling one-day bath conversions, walk-in tubs, wet space-only remodels, or full gut renovations are all competing against each other because the homeowners want to explore multiple options before committing. Speed, availability, and follow-through decide who gets a job just as much as price or products offered do. That crowded market with all different kinds of bathroom remodelers means that there is a real range in what a “bathroom job” means. A one-day bath conversion on only the wet space is a very different conversation than a full gut renovation with a homeowner picking out premium finishes. And both are vastly different from an accessibility upgrade or a walk-in tub conversion for an aging-in-place client. Whoever is answering your phone—whether it's a human or an AI agent—needs to be able to tell those conversations apart and ask the next right question, not just collect generic information in hopes a sales rep will do the rest. This guide is not here to help you generate more leads, but to give you concrete ways to convert more of the leads you’ve already generated. Make sure that once a homeowner decides to pick up the phone and choose a bathroom contractor, you’re ready for the call. Why the Phone Problem Is Getting More Expensive, Not Less Everyone hates their bathroom—at least that’s what the growth numbers for kitchen and bath remodeling tell us. The National Kitchen and Bath Association projects the U.S. kitchen and bath market at $228 billion in 2026, up 2.9%. GM Insights puts the North America bath remodeling market at roughly $75.6 billion in 2025, on a path to $96.2 billion by 2033. Globally, the bathroom remodeling market is estimated near $413 billion . The scale of growth in bathroom remodeling has made lead conversion harder, not easier. Where there may have only been a couple remodelers in a market ten years ago, there are now triple that number, and with the rise of private equity in home improvement, more and more money is being spent to acquire each lead. A bath remodeler spends real money to acquire each lead, whether it comes from an aggregator, an online form fill, or an after-hours voicemail that never got returned. Every missed lead is a real cost to the business, considering every dollar that went into generating it in the first place. Solving this problem with people is expensive and inconsistent. It’s not practical to staff a call center for a Saturday morning rush that might not happen. Hiring enough reps to call through a batch of 5,000 aged leads when you’re running a financing promotion doesn’t make sense. And you can’t guarantee every inbound call will be answered in seconds when your call center reps are already on the phone with someone else. The traditional fixes don’t make sense for business today. Hiring more CSRs helps until you hit slow season and then you’re paying people to sit by a quiet phone, or laying them off. Outsourcing to a third-party answering service gives a more personal touch than an automated voicemail, but the homeowner will still need a callback if they have specific questions that are outside the scope of the hired agency. This is where voice AI, and increasingly SMS AI, can make a big difference to your business and your customer. What Voice and SMS AI Actually Do for a Bath Remodeler Leaping AI works with a growing roster of bath remodeling companies, including Bath Experts and Lifetime Bath & Glass. The results these two companies have seen point to four specific ways AI agents change what a call center can do. Voice is the primary product, with SMS supporting the same kind of real conversations, just via a different channel. The most direct fix for remodelers is speed to lead. When a fresh lead comes in, whether it’s an online form fill, inbound call, or lead purchased from an aggregator, the faster you reach the homeowner, the higher the odds you will win the contract. Lifetime Bath & Glass set up an integration that routes leads from their vendors directly into Leaping AI within seconds of arriving. Their voice agents now reach out to those leads in about ten seconds and book an average of four to ten appointments a day, leading to up to 50% more appointments booked on peak days. After-hours coverage is usually the gap remodelers notice first. A homeowner researching a $20,000 bathroom project at 9 PM on a Wednesday after putting the kids to bed doesn’t have time to leave a voicemail and wait for a callback. They’re going to call the next name on their list until they can book. Voice AI picks up the call with the same tone, greeting, and structured conversation as your call center reps. It can gather the requisite information from the customer and book the appointment before the homeowner thinks to call a competitor. Every bath remodeler has a CRM full of old quote requests, leads that never closed, or contacts purchased from a lead aggregator that never picked up the phone. Activating those aged leads can be a gold mine for a remodeler looking to keep their cost per lead down. Bath Experts uses Leaping AI to work through both fresh and aged leads at scale. They make about 4,000 outbound calls with the AI agent a day, reaching about 15% of the people dialed, and booking roughly 5 in-home consultations a day. Each of those appointments is worth somewhere between $5,000 and $30,000 in potential revenue, which was just sitting in the CRM. Jay Shah, Head of Marketing at Bath Experts, put it simply: “Leaping AI helps us to systematically contact our real-time and aged leads lists and is booking us on average five incremental appointments a day.” Lead volume for a bath remodeler isn’t steady and can shift from market to market. It can spike from a marketing campaign, a change of season, or a special financing offer. Staffing for those peaks means paying people to sit idle during the valleys, or having to train temporary staff and hope they get your scripting right. Voice AI absorbs the routine, repeatable calls at scale, making it easy to meet your customer’s needs when they call and freeing up human CSRs to focus on the calls that require a person’s judgment. At Lifetime Bath, the top-performing CSR was promoted into a customer success manager role once the AI took over the routine outbound work. It’s important to consider the time to implement when looking at voice AI tools. Bath Experts was live in 30 days, seeing results that more than returned their investment. Lifetime Bath had its first three appointments on the calendar on the first day they went live. Time to value is one of the most important metrics to track when considering bringing in AI agents for the call center. Are the agents providing the same or more value than the human CSRs? How will you track that? Does the provider you’ve chosen have an implementation timeline? These are all questions a remodeler should ask when evaluating AI agent vendors. While a bath remodeler might start with a single use case, the others usually follow once the value of Voice and SMS agents has been proven. After-hours coverage is typically where a contractor will start, because it is the most obvious gap, but they will find themselves looking at aged lead reactivation or speed-to-lead once the technology has increased conversion on existing leads. The use cases all compound, increasing the ROI on the AI agents. What This Isn't Voice and SMS AI are not here to completely replace the call center. There will be customers who have questions that fall outside the standard scripting or need creative solutions. That’s where human CSRs should be spending their time and energy—building relationships and problem solving instead of handling routine scheduling calls. Tools like Leaping AI are also not simply virtual receptionists. Receptionists answer the phone and route calls to the appropriate resource. Voice AI agents can hold an actual conversation with a homeowner, follow your scripting and call flow to ask the right questions about their project, book the appointment on the calendar, and pass clear information back to the CRM for the wider team. Homeowners don’t want to wait for callbacks or on hold to be transferred to someone who can help them when they wrap their current call. Answering calls quickly and meeting customer needs the first time leads to a booked job. AI SMS agents are not the chatbots you encounter on every website that run on a strict script and will either send you a link to an article or make you wait for a person to contact you back during business hours. Every chat an SMS agent has with a customer is meant to be conversational, informative, and focused on booking the appointment. A major point of confusion for bath contractors evaluating AI agents is around the line between the agents and the CRM. A good voice or SMS AI tool should plug into the systems that already exist within the company, fitting into the tech stack of your industry, rather than forcing a major change to your operating system. Voice or SMS AI should plug into what’s already there, read the calendar, make the appointment, and pass clean information into the CRM for the rest of the team. That last point matters the most when you’re comparing AI agent vendors. Industry-agnostic AI tools or agents built for other verticals, like medical offices, don’t come with any foundation in bathroom remodeling. They don’t know how to structure a conversation to understand if a homeowner is looking to re-do just the wet space in their bathroom or do a full gut job. Companies seeing real results from AI agents, like Bath Experts and Lifetime Bath, chose a vendor built around how home remodelers actually operate, including their scripting and tech stack. Where to Go Deeper This is the starting point for a closer look at the specific parts of the phone problem facing bathroom remodelers today. In the articles that follow, we’ll cover why missed calls are quietly costing companies real booked jobs, how to tell voice AI, SMS AI, and chatbots apart before you buy the wrong one, what to check for when you’re evaluating a vendor for your call center, and what return on investment looks like, highlighting the use cases from real bath remodelers. Each one goes deeper than this overview can, and together with this article, they make up a full guide. If you read Leaping AI's earlier post on bath remodeling contractors automating their calls , this piece picks up where that one left off, with more specific numbers and a sharper look at each part of the problem. Seeing It in Your Call Center Having the biggest ad spend in your area isn’t going to make your company the fastest-growing bathroom remodeler in the market. The companies growing the fastest are the ones who maximize every single lead they’ve paid for, whether they’re generated through inbound or outbound activities. That starts with the phone. Answer it fast, cover calls 24/7, and work through the phone numbers sitting in your CRM. None of these tactics require a bigger team or a longer sales cycle to see results. Bath Experts had booked appointments within 30 days of kickoff. Lifetime Bath booked three new appointments on day one with voice AI. The pieces of this guide walk through exactly how, from the size of the problem, to the difference between the tools claiming to solve it, to what it takes to evaluate a vendor, to the real numbers behind the two bath remodelers already doing this today. Curious how you could convert more leads without adding headcount? Book a demo to see how Leaping AI would work in your call center.
